blocking.section: Decision outcome (Export and Logs rows, lines 49-50) and Confirmation (review checklist item, line 110)
blocking.issue: The ADR's export rule leaves out the one exception in the owning document. Observability rule O2 says bounded queues drop with a counter and 'only the audit export lags instead (OQ-observability-19)'. Control plane observability picks OpenTelemetry logs for the audit log: the leader exports batches keyed by Raft index, retries, 'lags and never drops'. The ADR states without exception that 'spans and logs pass Ruralz queues that drop' and that 'Code logs only through `log/slog`'. It never mentions OQ-observability-19, which is blocking for Planned (M2). Its review checklist would also flag the audit exporter, which has to call the OTLP log exporter directly and cannot go through `slog`. So the ADR does not match its owning document. It also hides that the System overview TB-12 row ('Drop on failure') is still being amended.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 50: "| Export | OTLP only when `Gateway.spec.telemetry.otlp.endpoint` is set, over TLS on boundary TB-12; spans and logs pass Ruralz queues that drop with `queue_full` or `export_error` counts; ..."; line 49: "Code logs only through `log/slog` via `internal/telemetry`"; line 110: "calling `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` outside `internal/telemetry`, MUST amend this ADR". Owning document, Observability principles O2: "Bounded span and log queues drop with a counter (TB-12); only the audit export lags instead (OQ-observability-19)"; Control plane observability: "Export retries, so it lags and never drops, unlike TB-12 (OQ-observability-19)". System overview TB-12: "Drop on failure".
blocking.fix: Add a Decision outcome row: '| Audit export | The Ruralz Control leader exports committed audit entries as OTLP logs from `internal/telemetry`, bypassing `slog` and the drop queues: batches keyed by Raft index, retried until acknowledged, a partial success counts as failure; lags and never drops, the TB-12 exception proposed in OQ-observability-19 | Planned (M2) |'. Scope the Logs row to 'Code logs only through `log/slog` via `internal/telemetry`, except the audit export'. Add 'except the audit export' to the Export row's drop sentence. Add a Bad consequence saying the audit export depends on the pre-stable OTLP log exporter and on OQ-observability-19, which is blocking for Planned (M2). Add a Figure 1 node for the audit export, drawn as a dashed edge to the OTLP exporter.

blocking.section: Decision drivers (One correlation key, line 31) and Consequences (line 90)
blocking.issue: The ADR's correlation key contradicts the owning document. Observability O6 makes the key the pair (`trace_id`, server `span_id`) and leaves telling apart requests that share a trace ID to OQ-observability-13. The ADR says the trace ID alone is 'the single correlation key'. A client that sends one sampled `traceparent` on several requests shares one trace ID across all of them, so the trace ID alone cannot pick out one access log record or problem document. The access log table in the owning document carries both `trace_id` and `span_id` (O6) for this reason.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 31: "**One correlation key**: the trace ID links spans, logs, exemplars and the `requestId` of every problem document"; line 90: "Good, because the trace ID is the single correlation key across spans, access log records, exemplars and `requestId`." Owning document O6: "(`trace_id`, server `span_id`) links logs, spans and exemplars; `requestId` carries the trace ID ([Data plane](03-data-plane.md#error-response-format)); the span ID is OQ-observability-13".
blocking.fix: Line 31: '**One correlation key**: (`trace_id`, server `span_id`) links spans, logs and exemplars, and the `requestId` of every problem document carries the trace ID; adding the span ID to `requestId` is OQ-observability-13 (rule O6 of [Observability](../architecture/10-observability.md#observability-principles))'. Line 90: 'Good, because one key, the trace ID with the server span ID (O6), correlates spans, access log records, exemplars and `requestId`.'

blocking.section: Decision outcome (paragraph after Chosen option, line 43), Consequences (lines 89 and 92), More information (line 140)
blocking.issue: What happens to logs at v1.47.0 disagrees with a depends_on document, and the ADR never states the end state. The tech stack Watch list, which the ADR links as the trigger, says the stable 'Logs SDK replaces the bridge'. The ADR's Consequences say call sites never change and 'bridge wiring inside `internal/telemetry` changes', so `slog` plus `otelslog` stays. The Decision outcome says logs 'move to the OpenTelemetry Logs API'. Foundation pack section 7 and the manifest decision say the bridge is used 'until' the Logs API is stable. An implementer cannot tell whether `otelslog` is temporary or permanent, and the Watch list row the ADR relies on says the opposite of its Consequences.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 43: "Logs move to the OpenTelemetry Logs API only after its stable release ... through a revisit of this ADR that the [Watch list](...) triggers"; line 89: "Good, because call sites never change when logs move to the stable Logs API: `log/slog` is the standard library"; line 92: "so bridge wiring inside `internal/telemetry` changes at v1.47.0". Tech stack Watch list: "| OTel Logs API | Release candidate (...) | v1.47.0 stable | Logs SDK replaces the bridge |". Pack section 7: "`slog` bridge (`otelslog`) for logs until the OTel Go Logs API is stable".
blocking.fix: State the end state once in Decision outcome, for example: 'At v1.47.0 the stable Logs API and SDK replace the release-candidate SDK behind the bridge; package call sites stay on `log/slog`, and `otelslog` stays inside `internal/telemetry` as the adapter from `slog` to the Logs API.' Add to More information: 'Proposed tech stack Watch list amendment: Fallback reads "Stable Logs SDK behind the `otelslog` bridge; `slog` call sites unchanged"'. If the intent is to drop the bridge instead, say that call sites move to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` and remove the line 89 consequence.

non_blocking.suggestion: The linked Banned imports section bans only `log`, and depguard confines only wazero, rueidis and `hashicorp/raft` to wrapper packages. Nothing yet keeps OpenTelemetry inside `internal/telemetry`. Reword to 'library churn SHOULD stay inside `internal/telemetry` (lint rule proposed in More information)', so the driver does not state a rule that does not exist yet as a fact.

'Proposed owning-document amendment' names Repository layout and conventions, which is not this ADR's owning document (Observability is). Write 'Proposed amendment to Repository layout and conventions (owner of depguard rules)', and include the OTLP exporter modules in the depguard rule.
